callers.method: Two scans, because neither alone is sufficient. (1) Cross-module: every relocs.txt under config/arm9/ was read and rows were accepted ONLY when the destination module was spelled exactly 'overlay(15)' -- the spelling in these files is overlay(15), NOT ov015, and a filter written against 'ov015' silently rejects everything and reports zero callers. Sanity check on that filter: 675 rows were REJECTED for naming a different destination module, so the filter is discriminating and not simply matching nothing. (2) Intra-overlay: a BL inside one overlay carries no relocation at all, so every B/BL word in ov015 .text was decoded and its sign-extended displacement resolved. Scan 2 is what found the 9 callers of func_ov015_02111fb8, which scan 1 also happened to list here but which would be invisible in a relocation-only scan of a typical overlay.
callers.external_callers: NONE. No module other than ov015 references any address in 0x02111ba0..0x02112290. This is a genuine result, not a broken filter -- the same scan, on the same run, positively reports 58 in-module references, and the rejected-row count above shows the module filter is live.
callers.entry_points: The class is reached only through the actor registry: the two profile records at 0x0211454c and 0x02114568 hold the two classInit pointers, and everything else is virtual dispatch through _ZTV at 0x0211458c. That is the normal shape for a spawned actor.
